1.explanation: In this example we configure TreeSelect with treeCheckable and multiple so checkboxes appear. We mark the node with value '4' as disableCheckbox. We then pass defaultValue={['4']}, which selects that disabled‐checkbox node by default. On initialization the component internally renders two identical tag elements for that single value (one for the disabled state and one for the selected state) using the same key '4'. React thus logs a duplicate-key warning, and you can visually see two identical tags. This minimal code reproduces the bug scenario from the original report.
1.bug_scenario: When a TreeSelect is rendered in multiple checkbox mode (treeCheckable & multiple) and one of the default selected values corresponds to a node whose checkbox is disabled (disableCheckbox) or the node itself is disabled, the placeholder input area shows that node’s label twice (duplicate tags) and React logs a "Warning: Encountered two children with the same key" error. In the screenshot, the “Input” node (value "4") is disableCheckbox: true, defaultValue is ["4"], and you see two identical “Input ×” tags and a duplicate-key warning in the console.
